title: Lightroom import
objective: Bring the photographs worked on in a Lightroom Classic catalog, or a folder of XMP sidecars, into the Luxforge catalog read-only, with their organization, their settings as one history entry each, a per-photograph report, re-mapping from the kept source text, and Lightroom's previews as first tiles.
context_summary: Planned from docs/design/lightroom-import.md, the contract every task follows; the owner decided all eleven questions on 2026-10-06 and did not authorize implementation, so nothing here starts until authorized. Phase 1 is TASK-001 to TASK-010, deliverable alone; TASK-011 is phase 2 (masks); TASK-012 is phase 3, mappings that land with later tools. The importer never writes to a Lightroom catalog, its previews, sidecars or originals; nothing from the owner's library enters the repository. It reuses the preset mapping and Lua reader, Develop's fingerprinting and event folders, the catalog's library changes and the rendered-preview fallback rule. Fidelity beyond value transfer comes from the Lightroom alignment design, not from this plan. Decisions: docs/decisions.md. Lightroom previews populate only the grid tier; imports have no import undo and keep the existing removal and send-back rules (owner, 2026-10-07). Lightroom commands, origins and the smoke scenario in this plan are proposed deliverables, not implemented interfaces.

tasks.description: Confirm the Lightroom Classic catalog format against the owner's catalog: the catalog version, the table and column subset the design names, the develop settings text including masks, the preview cache's index and file layout, and how the lock file and journal behave while Lightroom is open and closed.
extra_context: Read-only probe of a copy of the owner's .lrcat and its Previews.lrdata in a temporary directory; never open the owner's live files for writing and never commit them or anything read from them.

Record what is confirmed in a new docs/research/lightroom/catalog-format.md (tables, columns, value encodings such as pick, rating, colorLabels, orientation codes, masterImage and copyName; the Lua settings text, its size distribution and whether mask geometry, brush dabs and AI mask references are in it; previews.db and the .lrprev container; how a preview's currency against the last edit can be told), and correct the design where it differs.
Confirm that the preset parser's Lua subset (presets/lrtemplate.rs) reads the settings text, or list what it lacks.
This research task needs no code under crates/.

tasks.description: Build the read-only Lightroom catalog reader and a test-catalog generator: open read-only, refuse a locked catalog and an unverified version by name, stream photographs, files, folders, collections, keywords, snapshots, history-step counts and settings text, and parse the settings text into the preset mapping's setting table.
extra_context: New module under luxforge-core (for example crate::lightroom); SQLite through the pinned rusqlite, opened read-only with no journal written; rows streamed, never loaded whole.
The generator writes a catalog with exactly the schema subset TASK-001 confirmed, from a declarative description, for tests; it ships no Adobe-made file.
Bounds as preset import's: settings text size, nesting and value count refused with resource-limit; earlier process versions are identified for refusal by the mapping.

context_links.relevance: Lightroom's files; the confirmed schema subset is in the catalog-format note TASK-001 writes beside it.

acceptance_criteria: A generated catalog reads back to its description; a locked catalog and an unknown version are refused with their reasons; the catalog file's bytes hash the same before and after every read.
Settings text from the generator parses into the same setting table an equivalent XMP sidecar gives.

tasks.description: Map one Lightroom photograph to a Luxforge edit and report: the preset mapping for global settings plus the per-photo rows (crop, user orientation, lens profile switch, camera profile to the look, perspective and everything else reported), built as one composite of module actions with every setting accounted for in the report.
extra_context: Extend the presets mapping table rather than adding a second one; per-photo rows are marked as not presettable so preset import keeps excluding them.

The crop conversion (CropTop/Left/Bottom/Right and CropAngle with the photo's orientation into the crop module's normalized rotated box) is frozen by a small study against Lightroom exports of known crops the owner makes once; record the round's figures in the design.
Camera Matching profiles map to Standard with an approximate note until Match camera exists; Adobe Color and Adobe Standard map to Standard.
The report keeps preset import's shape and adds crop, orientation, lens and look rows, and which rule (value transfer or a calibrated conversion) each mapped row used.

Detail globals and manual perspective remain unsupported by the preset mapping despite both modules being delivered; their mappings need the measured alignment, not delivery of those tools. RAW white balance already has an uncalibrated chromaticity conversion; its calibrated preset conversion lands in the alignment RAW white-balance round.

apply-preset accepts only presettable field patches and at most 16 steps; crop, orientation, lens and look are not all presettable. Build the importer's bounded one-entry transaction through the shared module planning and validation APIs, without weakening public preset eligibility or claiming apply-preset already supports per-photo actions.

Per-photo actions validate and commit with the globals in one importer entry, while preset import retains its existing eligibility and bounds; first preparation cannot append an automatic lens entry after the imported head has moved.

tasks.description: Run the import as a job: lightroom.inspect and lightroom.import over a catalog on the library lane, importing the photographs worked on, fingerprinting through Develop's path, catalog folders by event, collections and groups, ratings and labels as collections, virtual copies and snapshots as named versions, duplicates linked with a Lightroom version, missing originals and unsupported kinds reported, journalled bounded parts with no import undo, idempotent re-runs and cancellation; with lightroom.report and lightroom.imports.
extra_context: Index the folders of the photographs in scope before computing their events, so catalog folders come from events as Develop's do; an event with a catalog folder reuses it.
Nothing on the owner thread but commits; paths are read by the worker. Each photograph's edit is its own history entry, `Imported from Lightroom` by the system actor.
Register every method in the command registry with its schema.

Keep MAX_LIBRARY_BATCH (50,000 library items, not photographs) and the prepared-batch bounds; stream and commit explicit parts as Develop does, recording retry identities. Each completed photograph, its import entry and provenance are atomic, with no half-import on failure or cancellation.

There is no import undo (owner, 2026-10-07). Existing library undo and asset.send-back retain their guards against entries beyond Original, versions and collections; Remove uses the existing catalog rule.

version.create names an existing retained entry and does not create a branch. The importer must append validated entries branched from Original for copies, snapshots and linked Lightroom versions, naming them without moving an existing photograph's current head. Reuse the append-only entry and version invariants; do not fake detached entries by temporarily navigating the client's head.

context_links.label: Catalog design
context_links.relevance: Developing picks, events, folders, collections and library changes.

acceptance_criteria: Over generated catalogs: only photographs worked on are imported; folders follow events; collections, ratings, labels, copies and snapshots land as decided; duplicates link; missing originals are reported; a re-run imports only what is new; a cancel keeps finished photographs and nothing partial; no import undo is exposed; existing send-back and library-undo guards refuse removal of retained edits, versions or collections without changing data.
The Lightroom catalog, its sidecars and the originals hash the same before and after, cancelled and failed runs included.

An import beyond one library part stays within the item and preparation bounds, retries no part twice, and preserves every completed photograph on cancellation. Copies, snapshots and linked versions survive reopen branched from Original, with the master or existing current head preserved.

steps: Run the import tests over generated catalogs and originals from the fixture generator.
expected_results: Every import and library test passes.

tasks.description: Use Lightroom's previews as the imported photographs' first grid tiles only: read each new photograph's largest current Lightroom preview, fit it upright within the 512 px grid tier with origin lightroom, report thumbnail and replace it by the tile service's render; reject a stale preview. The large tier follows the existing camera-preview and rendered-tier path.
extra_context: Reads happen on the extraction workers; the Lightroom preview cache is opened read-only and never written. origin lightroom and its source-preview key are new cache shapes this task adds, not existing API values.

Only a newly imported photograph whose imported entry is current gets a Lightroom grid row. A linked photograph gets a named version and no Lightroom preview row, preserving its current head and previews.

Use the camera-preview write guard: never replace a rendered grid or reseed Lightroom rows after a render, re-run, edit, generation bump or index rebuild. A source-preview row has no drawn_by renderer; renderer-generation invalidation applies to rendered rows only. The import job alone seeds it, and stale-entry collection still removes it.

A stale or missing Lightroom preview is not written, so the camera-grid extraction remains available. A Lightroom grid row must not suppress extraction of the independent 2048 px large camera tier. The grid origin is shown in Select and filmstrip cells; Develop's canvas, Compare and the large-tier loupe never receive a Lightroom row.
Replacing rendered tiers use the owner's tile service, the desktop GPU tile worker or the reference fallback, and record drawn_by and the reference reason.
acceptance_criteria: A Lightroom preview becomes only the new current entry's grid row with origin lightroom and thumbnail state, is replaced by a rendered grid and never reseeded; linked photographs get no Lightroom row. A stale preview falls back to the camera grid.

The large camera/render tier stays independent; Select loupe, Develop canvas and Compare show no Lightroom preview. Races with camera extraction and rendering preserve origin priority, and generation bumps and index rebuilds do not reseed the import preview.
Replacing rendered tiers name their renderer and any reference reason; new origin and key shapes round-trip through the index and API with current-format cache rules.

steps: Run preview-cache tests over generated Lightroom previews, linked versions, stale entries, renderer-generation changes, rebuilds, camera extraction and a replacing-render race.

tasks.description: Re-map from Lightroom: lightroom.remap over selected photographs runs the current mapping on the stored text and commits a new entry only where the result differs.
extra_context: Never automatic. A batch follows batch.apply-preset's job, retry and report rules.
acceptance_criteria: An unchanged mapping commits nothing; a changed mapping commits one entry per changed photograph; retries apply nothing twice.

tasks.description: Import a folder of originals with XMP sidecars through the same job, mapping and report, for people without a catalog.
extra_context: Without a catalog there are no collections, picks, ratings or copies: every original with a sidecar holding develop settings is in scope.
acceptance_criteria: A generated sidecar folder imports with the same reports an equivalent catalog gives; sidecars and originals are unchanged.

tasks.description: Phase 2: import Lightroom's masks: linear, radial, brush and range components with intersect, subtract and invert, and their supported local adjustments as masked Basic and Presence layers, with every unsupported component and adjustment reported and nothing silently omitted.
extra_context: Brush dabs go to the stroke store; density other than 100 is reported. A radial that Lightroom applies outside gets Invert.
AI masks are reported as not imported until model-based Select exists; their adjustments are reported as not applied.

Import transactions validate every mask and local module action through the shared core APIs; apply-preset is global-only and does not create masks or masked layers. Keep decoded strokes and prepared commits bounded for a photograph with many components.

context_links.label: Masking design
context_links.relevance: Mask kinds, algebra and the stroke store.

acceptance_criteria: Each mask mapping has a test from settings to mask and layers; a mask with no supported component is not created and its adjustments are reported; the rendered scenario shows an imported masked photograph.

steps: Run the mask mapping tests and the scenario.

tasks.description: Phase 3: map Camera Matching, repair and AI settings as their capabilities land, and delivered tools once measured: Camera Matching profiles to Match camera, spot removal to Clone and Heal, AI masks recomputed through Select, and global and local Detail and manual perspective once Lightroom alignment has measured them; existing imports reach them through Re-map.
extra_context: Blocked on the capabilities by name: Match camera (RAW looks phase 2), Clone and Heal (Corrections), model-based Select (AI editing), and the Detail and perspective alignment studies. Each mapping lands as its capability does.

Detail and Lens and perspective are delivered; only their Lightroom mappings and measurement are outstanding. Camera Matching is in phase 3, matching this task, and maps to Standard with an approximate report until Match camera lands.
acceptance_criteria: Each added mapping has its tests and report rows; Re-map applies it to existing imports.

steps: Run the mapping tests as each lands.
